- **self**: Canary and Shadow-Traffic Comparison (12/6)

## Definitions

- [statement] Shadow traffic is not automatically side-effect-free. A state-changing request may execute on both versions, and shared state such as a cache can alter or contaminate performance measurements. Isolate candidate data and downstream effects, or make replayed operations safe to repeat. (high confidence) — https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/mirror-production-traffic-to-test-environment-with-vpc-traffic-mirroring/ · keywords: Canary and Shadow-Traffic Comparison · also: https://sre.google/workbook/canarying-releases/

## How it works

- [statement] A canary routes a controlled share of production traffic to a changed version while the control serves the rest. Users in the canary slice receive candidate responses, so defects can affect that slice; teams compare candidate and control signals and can stop or roll back when the candidate regresses. (high confidence) — https://medium.com/netflix-techblog/automated-canary-analysis-at-netflix-with-kayenta-3260bc7acc69 · keywords: Canary and Shadow-Traffic Comparison · also: https://sre.google/workbook/canarying-releases/, https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/mirror-production-traffic-to-test-environment-with-vpc-traffic-mirroring/
- [statement] AWS VPC Traffic Mirroring is not universally zero-impact: AWS documentation says mirrored packets count toward source-instance bandwidth and may be dropped when bandwidth or packet-rate limits are exceeded. The AWS blog's no-performance-impact statement is specific to its out-of-band architecture and should not be generalized to every mirroring setup. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/mirroring/traffic-mirroring-network-limitations.html · keywords: Canary and Shadow-Traffic Comparison · also: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/mirror-production-traffic-to-test-environment-with-vpc-traffic-mirroring/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Shadow runs exercise the candidate on copied production inputs but cannot show how users respond to candidate answers because only the incumbent response reaches them. Replayed state-changing requests can duplicate effects; AWS calls out idempotency, and InfoQ recommends read-only replicas or staging data for downstream state. (high confidence) — https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/mirror-production-traffic-to-test-environment-with-vpc-traffic-mirroring/ · keywords: Canary and Shadow-Traffic Comparison · also: https://www.infoq.com/articles/microservices-traffic-mirroring-istio-vpc/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] In Envoy v1.36.11, RequestMirrorPolicy mirrors all requests when runtime_fraction is unset and can restrict mirroring to a configured fraction when it is set. Sampling can limit candidate load, with the trade-off that fewer requests are measured. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-01) — https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/v1.36.11/api-v3/config/route/v3/route_components.proto · keywords: Canary and Shadow-Traffic Comparison

## Facts and statements

- [statement] A canary routes a portion of live requests to a candidate, so some users receive candidate responses; shadow traffic copies production requests to the candidate while the incumbent serves the client and the shadow response is discarded. (high confidence) — https://medium.com/netflix-techblog/automated-canary-analysis-at-netflix-with-kayenta-3260bc7acc69 · keywords: Canary and Shadow-Traffic Comparison · also: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/mirror-production-traffic-to-test-environment-with-vpc-traffic-mirroring/
- [statement] A useful canary comparison uses a baseline running the production version and configuration, created alongside the candidate; match deployment time, instance count, traffic type, and traffic amount. Comparing against long-running production can confound results through cache warmup, heap, or load-balancing differences. (high confidence) — https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/devops-sre/canary-analysis-lessons-learned-and-best-practices-from-google-and-waze · keywords: Canary and Shadow-Traffic Comparison · also: https://medium.com/netflix-techblog/automated-canary-analysis-at-netflix-with-kayenta-3260bc7acc69
- [statement] Canary analysis should compare configured baseline and candidate time-series metrics that represent service health, including latency, errors, and saturation. Netflix's Kayenta description validates and cleans metric data, classifies individual metrics, and aggregates results; it describes Mann–Whitney U confidence intervals as its primary comparison algorithm. (high confidence) (verified as of 2018-04-10) — https://medium.com/netflix-techblog/automated-canary-analysis-at-netflix-with-kayenta-3260bc7acc69 · keywords: Canary and Shadow-Traffic Comparison · also: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/gcp/introducing-kayenta-an-open-automated-canary-analysis-tool-from-google-and-netflix, https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/devops-sre/canary-analysis-lessons-learned-and-best-practices-from-google-and-waze
- [statement] Google and Waze recommend validating a canary analysis configuration with known-good and known-bad app versions, and running an A/A check with the same version on both sides that should pass. (low confidence) — https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/devops-sre/canary-analysis-lessons-learned-and-best-practices-from-google-and-waze · keywords: Canary and Shadow-Traffic Comparison
- [statement] Google and Waze's Spinnaker guidance recommends at least 50 time-series data points per metric for statistically relevant canary analysis; depending on monitoring granularity, this can require several hours of analysis. (low confidence) (verified as of 2019-01-14) — https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/devops-sre/canary-analysis-lessons-learned-and-best-practices-from-google-and-waze · keywords: Canary and Shadow-Traffic Comparison
- [statement] Shadowing leaves the stable version on the client response path and sends a copy of each selected request to the candidate; the candidate response is discarded and does not delay the primary response. This exercises the candidate on real request inputs without exposing its output to users. (high confidence) — https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/mirror-production-traffic-to-test-environment-with-vpc-traffic-mirroring/ · keywords: Canary and Shadow-Traffic Comparison · also: https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/v1.36.11/api-v3/config/route/v3/route_components.proto, https://sre.google/workbook/canarying-releases/
- [statement] Canary metrics should be broken down by candidate and control population, and their aggregation intervals should fit within the canary duration. Service-wide metrics can dilute a regression affecting a small traffic slice, while a time window longer than the canary can mix unrelated events into the comparison. (high confidence) — https://sre.google/workbook/canarying-releases/ · keywords: Canary and Shadow-Traffic Comparison · also: https://medium.com/netflix-techblog/automated-canary-analysis-at-netflix-with-kayenta-3260bc7acc69
